- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 3–7% to match true decline.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average before forecasting to reduce overshoot.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model often lags in correction; add 1–2 day lag in price drop prediction.
- In high volatility periods (sentiment extremes), model tends to overfit recent trends; apply mean reversion bias: if forecast > 2σ above recent mean, cap at mean + 1.5σ.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses long-term mean reversion; if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish, forecast should align with 10–15 day moving average rather than 30-day trend.
